flashcards.definition: Voluntary, cross-striated, multinucleated syncytial muscle fibers under somatic motor neural control.
Involuntary, non-striated, uninucleated spindle-shaped (fusiform) cells lining visceral organs under autonomic control.
Involuntary, cross-striated, single-nucleated branched cardiocytes joined by specialized intercalated discs.
Functional contractile unit of myofibrils bounded between two adjacent Z-lines.
Dark central sarcomere band formed by thick myosin filaments; length remains constant during contraction.
Light sarcomere band containing thin actin filaments; shortens during muscle contraction.
Stores Ca2+; nerve depolarization triggers Ca2+ release to bind Troponin C, moving Tropomyosin away from actin active sites.
High myoglobin and mitochondria content; rich capillary supply; slow contraction speed; high fatigue resistance.
Low myoglobin; high sarcoplasmic reticulum; relies on anaerobic glycolysis; fast contraction with rapid fatigue.
Endomysium (encloses single fiber), Perimysium (encloses fascicle bundle), Epimysium (encloses whole muscle belly).
Junctional structures in cardiac muscle containing Fascia Adherens, Desmosomes, and Gap Junctions for electrical syncytium.
Single-unit (visceral, gap junctions, myogenic e.g. gut); Multi-unit (neurogenic, independent units e.g. arrector pili).
